title: A forest is trees standing apart in bands along the way, with open ground between
rule: Plant Episode Two's woods thin and uneven: most trees alone (no other within 160), the nearest neighbour 150 to 300 away, 2 to 10 trees in a square 1000 a side; few on the path's edge (within 128 of the walk), the thickest band 256 to 1024 off it, thinning beyond 1024 where cards take over; and leave about half of the 512 squares with no tree at all. A few small clumps of three to five, never an even scatter. Our forests were planted and thinned at the owner's asking: ask the owner first before changing how thick they stand.
why: Ten EP2 forest maps (21 November): nearest other tree, median 148 (ep2_outland_05), 154 (01), 165 (10a), 206 (10), 211 (12a), 244 (12), 252 (09), 261 (06a), 294 (07), 298 (08). Alone within 160: 54 to 97% (06a 85%, 07 97%, 12 81%); only 01, 05 and 10a have a quarter in groups of three or more. Trees per 1000x1000 by distance from the AI nodes: 0-128 0.1 to 7, 128-256 0.5 to 8, 256-512 2.2 to 10.6, 512-1024 1.8 to 6.4, beyond 1024 0 to 3. Of 512 squares with ground in the trees' box, 44 to 82% hold no tree (10a 0.44, 12 0.47, 10 0.48, 01 0.57, 06a 0.59, 07 0.73). Ours (map_forest.py Forest.plant, a 150 grid kept at 0.23 to 0.48, 0.64 on the ridge): about 14 a 1000 square over the valley (21 before the pond and paths), 28 on the ridge band, median gap 132, 27% alone.
how: map_forest.py: plant by distance from the trail and the gate's way in (bands as above) rather than an even grid; a Poisson-disc spacing of about 150 with a gap test, a clump now and then (three to five within 120); leave whole 512 squares open; keep the ridge's own band for the cards (valve-forest-border). Count and print alone share, median gap and empty squares with each build.
check: proposed: map_forest prints the median gap between trees (want 150 to 300), the share alone within 160 (want over a half) and the share of 512 squares with no tree (want 0.4 to 0.8)

title: Trees sink into the ground, deeper on a slope, and some lean
rule: Set every tree's origin below the ground under it: 5 to 13 on level ground, 20 to 50 on a slope, so no root shows over the downhill side. Lean a tenth to a half of the trees 3 to 11 degrees (a few to 25), more on slopes and at the forest's edge, never a cut tree upright on a slope. Turn them on 15 degree steps or freely. Trees are solid static props that cast shadows and fade out between about 4200 and 7000. Pieces already built keep their look: ask the owner first before changing them.
why: EP2 (21 November), origin minus the displaced ground under it: median -4.7 (01), -9.2 (05), -9.6 (06a), -10.5 (07), -6.6 (08), -9.6 (09), -11.9 (10), -10.4 (10a), -6.4 (12), -13.3 (12a); the deepest tenth -20 to -54. Leaning more than 2 degrees: 01 43%, 05 61%, 06 57%, 08 23%, 12 20%, 10a 15%, 06a 14%, 10 10%, 07 7%, 09 0%; median lean 4 to 11, 90th 10 to 27. Yaw on 15 degree steps 53 to 99%. fademaxdist: 07 7000 on 296 of 313, 01 5000 to 5200, 10a 2200 on 164 small ones and 4200 to 5200 on the rest; disableshadows 0 on every tree; solid 6. Ours: 8 down everywhere, no lean, yaw on 5, fade 2800 to 3400.
how: map_forest.py Forest.static for trees: sink = 6 + 0.25 x the ground's drop across the trunk (from the height function at 32 each side), lean = 3 to 9 degrees for one tree in five (one in three on slopes over 0.4), leaning downhill; fade (4200, 6000).
check: proposed: map_forest checks every tree is at least 4 below the lowest of five ground heights under its trunk

title: A forest's edge is cards past the last trees, a clip on the slope and painted hills in the sky
rule: Stop players in the woods without a wall they can see: an invisible player clip laid along the top of a slope or among the last trees (tall, 200 to 600 long, turned with the ground); past the last real trees (about 1000 to 2000 from the walk) flat tree cards (tree_pine_card_cluster_01/02, tree_deciduous_card_01, tree_pine_tall_cluster_01), not solid; and the far distance painted on brushes in the 3D skybox (mountainrange materials), with no props there at all. Our forests are held by a ridge 440 high and planted thickest on it: ask the owner first before trading the ridge's trees for cards.
why: EP2 (21 November): cards 3 to 42 a map (12: 42, 09: 27, 07: 22, 10a: 21), median 870 to 2340 from the AI nodes, 500 to 1200 beyond the nearest real tree, solid 0 on 80 to 100% in most maps; in 12 no real tree stands more than 512 from the walk, cards stand beyond. toolsplayerclip brushes: 26 to 177 a forest map, median 54 to 570 from the nodes, height median 336 to 896, length median 192 to 576, half off the axes. Steep displacement 0.13 to 1.43 of the flat area. The 3D skybox of 01, 05 to 10 and 12a holds no tree prop: brushes with mountainrange_far_00c/02c/04c, mountains_skybox02, groundplane_01c (8 to 44 brushes, 0 to 11 displacements). ep2_outland_01 paints trees onto its cliff displacements with clifftrees_cardboard01a and 02a (1,562 of displaced area beside cliff03a/04a).
how: map_forest.py: a ring of card props on the ridge's far side, 1000 to 1500 from the trail, solid 0; a player clip along the ridge top; keep real trees inside it. The skybox is the city's (map_merge): no change.
check: proposed: map_forest lists card props within 600 of the trail (they show their flatness up close)

title: The forest floor: ferns along the path, rocks and logs tilted, grass from the ground's own material
rule: Ground cover comes from the ground material's detail sprites, switched off (a no-sprite twin of the material) where people walk; fern props are few (a tenth to a half of the tree count) and line the path's edges, not the tree feet; rocks lie tilted (four in ten to three in four more than 5 degrees) and part sunk, 150 to 350 from the nearest tree; logs and fallen trees lie tilted, stumps near the trees. Nothing small is solid. Pieces already built keep their look: ask the owner first before changing them.
why: EP2 (21 November): every map sets detailmaterial detail/detailsprites and detailvbsp detail.vbsp; walked ground in blendgrassdirt01_noprop (07: 14,763 against 6,246 by area for blendgrassdirt01; 10a 6,574 against 1,099). Plants (fern01 nearly always, fern01lg, grass_cluster03a, shrub_01a) 6 to 155 a map, 0.04 to 0.5 per tree, solid 0 on all, median 70 to 370 from the nodes and 110 to 500 from a tree. Rocks 17 to 174 a map (rockcluster01/02, rock_coast02a to h, rocks_large*_veg, forestrock_cluster01/02), tilted over 5 degrees 41 to 76%, median 160 to 340 from a tree. Logs and stumps 2 to 133 (tree_stump01, fallentree01/02, fallentree_dry01/02, forest_log01), tilted 39 to 100%. Ours: 170 plants a forest (0.74 per tree) anywhere not steep, 34 rocks and 12 logs, none tilted.
how: map_forest.py: plants mostly within 64 to 256 of the trail; rocks pitch and roll 5 to 25 degrees for two in three, sunk 10 to 20; logs rolled to the slope. Check the ground material has detail sprites, and use a no-sprite twin on the trail if one exists (ask before adding materials).
check: proposed: map_forest prints the share of rocks tilted (want 0.4 to 0.75) and of plants within 256 of the trail

title: Antlion caves: tunnels about 250 wide and 200 high, opening now and then into chambers
rule: Make a natural cave as about three parts tunnel to one part chamber: tunnels 220 to 300 across at the narrowest (a tenth down to 120 to 180), 160 to 240 high (a quarter over 320); chambers 512 or more across and 1000 to 1800 long. Every wall, roof and floor displaced. Our cave and nest are built and walked: ask the owner first before changing their size.

In tunnels under 384 wide: 60 to 74%; in chambers 512 or more: 17 to 20%; the longest way across, 75th percentile 1500 to 1840. Ours: the cave hung on a square 320 by 320 (CaveForest.HALF, TALL); the nest 345 wide in its narrows and up to 760 in its chambers (NestTube radius 150 to 330), chambers about a third of its length.
how: map_forest.py: if the owner wants it, narrow the cave's tunnels to about 260 between the mouth and the chamber and lower them to about 220; NestTube: radius about 120 in the narrows.

title: Antlion grubs lie in twos to fours on the walls, each group with a small yellow light

Our nest has its grubs one at a time: ask the owner first.

Lights within 160 of a grub: 43 (01a), 60 (03), 47 (04), 18 of 24 (style room); median 30 to 43 from the grub in 01a and the style room; colour 255 245 157 on 38 of 43 (01a), 57 of 60 (03); brightness 30 to 80; spawnflags 4 on most. title: A building decays by bending: boards, roof tiles and tin sheets turned to displacements
rule: To show a timber or tin building gone to ruin, keep its frame but bend its skin: make boards, roof tiles, corrugated sheets and brick faces into small power 2 displacements and sag them (roofs down, boards bowed, sheets buckled), break the boards shorter, turn more of them off the square, and make the loose ones func_detail. Do it on the walls and roofs, not by deleting them. Pieces already built keep their look: ask the owner first before changing them.
why: styleguide_barn_deterioration against styleguide_barn (21 November), both 620 wood brushes: 539 displacements against 0 (power 2 on 479, 3 on 24, 4 on 36; woodfloor005a 212, tileroof003a 68, metalwall014a 50, brickwall020a 33; board strips 153 by 30 to 39; 354 on walls, 95 on ceilings, 90 on floors); off the axes 59% against 45%; func_detail 75% against 20%; board length median 62 against 111. styleguide_inn bends shingles (woodshingles002a 16) and stone (stonewall050g 18) with 139 power 2 displacements; outland_building_large_01 breaks brick edges with 40 small ones (21x6, 24x6).
how: For the infestation quarter or a ruined farm piece: a 'decay' pass in map tools that turns chosen faces into power 2 displacements with a sag (down 4 to 16 at the middle of a span) and bows boards 2 to 6.
